title: The Bihar Illegal Sand Mining Scam
dek: A Rajasthan-based company allegedly excavated ₹131 crore worth of river sand from Bihar's Banka district over seven years without paying royalties — a network the ED traced from Patna to Delhi and Jaipur using satellite imaging.

heroStat.label: value of sand the ED estimates was illegally extracted in Banka district, Bihar, between 2015-16 and 2022-23

promise.quote: Riverbed sand mining in Bihar will occur only under valid state mining licences, with royalties paid on all extraction, protecting river ecosystems and state revenue alike.
promise.madeBy: Bihar mining and geology department regulatory framework
promise.role: State regulator of riverbed sand mining licences and royalty collection
promise.context: The ED's investigation centres on Mahadev Enclave Private Limited, a company controlled by Ashok Chandak and his son Raghav Chandak of Sriganganagar, Rajasthan, alleged to have illegally mined sand from rivers in Banka district over several financial years.

target.description: Sand mining conducted strictly within licensed limits, with royalties paid to the state exchequer on all extracted volumes, and no unlicensed commercial exploitation of riverbeds.
target.standard: Bihar Minor Mineral Concession Rules and state mining royalty regulations.

reality.description: The ED alleges that Mahadev Enclave Private Limited illegally extracted sand from rivers in Banka district, Bihar, between financial years 2015-16 and 2022-23, with the value of illegally mined sand estimated at over ₹131 crore, causing losses to the state exchequer through unpaid royalties. The agency's case draws on a geospatial analysis commissioned from IIT Patna in October 2024, which found evidence of large-scale illegal excavation. On 17 July 2026, the ED conducted searches at eight locations across Banka and Patna in Bihar, Delhi-NCR, and Jaipur and Sri Ganganagar in Rajasthan under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, seizing ₹1.53 crore in cash. The ED has also formally flagged the ₹131 crore scam to the Bihar government and sought a fresh FIR.

gap.metricLabel: Estimated value of illegally mined sand vs. cash seized in ED raids
gap.note: Cash seized in a single round of raids is a small fraction of the estimated extraction value, which largely reflects lost royalty revenue rather than cash the company is presumed to be holding on hand.

money.notes: ₹131 crore is the ED's estimate of illegally mined sand value over eight years; ₹1.53 crore in cash was seized in the July 2026 raids.

timeline.label: Alleged illegal mining begins
timeline.detail: Mahadev Enclave Private Limited allegedly begins large-scale unlicensed sand extraction in Banka district.

timeline.label: IIT Patna geospatial analysis commissioned
timeline.detail: The ED's Patna office requests IIT Patna to analyse sand ghats in Banka district, later finding evidence of large-scale illegal excavation.

timeline.label: ED raids eight locations
timeline.detail: Simultaneous searches are conducted across Bihar, Delhi-NCR, and Rajasthan; ₹1.53 crore in cash is seized.

timeline.label: ED seeks fresh FIR from Bihar government
timeline.detail: The agency formally flags the ₹131 crore scam to state authorities and requests a fresh FIR be registered.

verdict.summary: Preliminary verdict, pending fuller research: the ED's use of satellite/geospatial analysis to quantify illegal riverbed mining is a notable investigative approach, but the case remains at the raid-and-referral stage, with no criminal case yet formally registered by Bihar authorities as of the most recent reporting reviewed.
verdict.reasoning: This entry is based on a handful of independent reports of the July 2026 ED raids and referral; it has not been possible to confirm whether Bihar authorities have since registered the fresh FIR the ED sought.

incomplete: This is a stub entry; whether the Bihar government has registered the fresh FIR the ED requested has not been confirmed.
Whether any arrests have followed the July 2026 raids has not been tracked.

A separate, larger reported figure of a ₹2,407 crore illegal sand mining network across Hyderabad, Jaipur, and Coimbatore may or may not be linked to this same company; this has not been reconciled here.
